newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia securities, commodities commissions merge.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia securities, commodities commissions merge.

text.p: The Malaysian Securities Commission (SC) said on Wednesday it had merged with the Commodities Trading Commission (CTC), resulting in the regulation of commodity futures coming under the purview of the SC.
With the merger, the Kuala Lumpur Commodity Exchange (KLCE), the Malaysian Futures Clearing Corporation (MFCC) and their members will be regulated by the SC.

The merger stems from the government's decision to rationalise the regulatory framework to create efficiencies in regulation and reduce costs of compliance for market participants, SC chairman Munir Abdul Majid said in a statement.
The SC and CTC merger affects three exchanges - the KLCE, the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange (KLOFFE) and the Malaysia Monetary Exchange (MME).

"With one regulatory agency supervising three exchanges, it sets the stage for further economies to be achieved through the rationalisation of the activities of market institutions and participants," Munir said.
"It would be in the interest of the industry for the exchanges to integrate," he said.
Munir said the current development plans for the capital market will now also include the commodity futures industry.
